race.name: Utrecht Ultra XL
race.tagline: A 1,600-kilometer self-supported road ultra from Utrecht through the Vosges and Flemish Ardennes

vitals.location: Utrecht, Netherlands (loop through Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, and France)
vitals.date_specific: 2026: August 1 (mass start 08:00; finish deadline August 7 at 22:00)
vitals.start_format: Mass start; solo and pairs categories; continuously GPS-tracked
vitals.registration: 2026 entry closed; no 2027 registration cycle published
vitals.entry_fee: EUR200 (2026, including tracker and staffed Vosges checkpoint)
vitals.feed_zones: Self-supported commercial resupply; one staffed Vosges checkpoint offers beds and showers

climate.description: August conditions range from exposed lowland heat and rain to cooler nights and fast-changing weather in the Vosges.
challenges: Nearly seven days of weather exposure across five countries
Cold or wet overnight conditions in the Vosges
Wind exposure on the Dutch and Belgian return

terrain.surface: Approximately 99% tarmac with short mandatory gravel sectors and cobbled climbs
features: 218 km Vosges parcours with nearly 5,000 m of climbing

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: First-edition self-supported road ultra scored from the organizer's published 1,600 km, 14,000 m, 158-hour course and EUR200 entry. The gran_fondo discipline is retained for schema compatibility; catalog_flags records the ultra-distance taxonomy mismatch.

key_climbs.name: Vosges checkpoint parcours
key_climbs.description: The organizer's hardest mandatory block, crossing the Vosges from the northern hills into sustained mountain terrain.

course_description.character: A partly free-routed, partly fixed 1,600 km road ultra. Riders leave Utrecht together, choose their own commercially supportable lines between three checkpoints, and complete mandatory parcours along the Luxembourg-Germany border, through the Vosges, and across the cobbled hills near Oudenaarde before following the fixed return through Zeeland.
course_description.signature_challenge: The 218 km Vosges parcours: nearly 5,000 m of climbing inside one mandatory block, reached after riders have already navigated hundreds of self-supported kilometers.
suffering_zones: The Luxembourg-Germany border parcours — river valleys and repeated climbs after the opening free-route section
The 218 km Vosges block — nearly 5,000 m of climbing, mountain weather, and a staffed refuge checkpoint
Oudenaarde and the Flemish cobbled climbs — rough, punchy terrain late in the race
The fixed Zeeland-to-Utrecht return — exposed lowland kilometers against the closing 158-hour clock

logistics.airport: Amsterdam Schiphol is the main international gateway; Utrecht is directly connected by train.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Book Utrecht accommodation before and after the event; during the race, only services commercially available to every rider are allowed and cannot be pre-booked before the start.
logistics.transport: The event starts and finishes in Utrecht. The entry includes a GPS tracker, pre-start bike check, secure storage, a staffed Vosges checkpoint, and a finish party.
logistics.food: Commercial self-resupply throughout; no private resupply or outside support.

history.origin_story: Introduced as the longer sister race to the 1,000 km Utrecht Ultra, adding substantially more climbing and a deep Vosges parcours while retaining the organizer's mixed fixed/free-routing format.
history.reputation: A new extension of an established Dutch self-supported ultra organizer rather than a long-running standalone classic.

biased_opinion.verdict: A Smart Step Up From Utrecht Ultra
biased_opinion.summary: Utrecht Ultra XL takes the original race's approachable route-choice concept and turns it into a serious trans-European ultra: 1,600 km, 14,000 m, a 158-hour clock, a 218 km Vosges block, and cobbles near Oudenaarde. The EUR200 entry is unusually strong value for a tracker, staffed mountain checkpoint, storage, media, and finish support. Its limitation is history: 2026 is the inaugural edition, so the course has not yet accumulated the repeat-edition evidence of Europe's established ultras.
strengths: A clearly differentiated 1,600 km course rather than a token extension of the standard Utrecht Ultra
The Vosges and Flemish mandatory parcours create real mountain and classics-road specificity
EUR200 includes tracker rental, bike check, secure storage, a staffed checkpoint with beds and showers, and the finish party
Solo and pairs categories preserve a genuine self-supported racing format
weaknesses: The inaugural edition has no multi-year reliability or route-history record
Free routing makes the exact rider distance and climbing dependent on navigation choices
No private support, no pre-booked lodging, and only one staffed refuge make logistics part of the competition
The closing cobbles and exposed Dutch return arrive after more than 1,000 km
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A well-designed, good-value European road ultra for riders who want materially more mountain work than Utrecht Ultra without stepping all the way to a continent-crossing race.

final_verdict.one_liner: A strong-value 1,600 km self-supported ultra with a real Vosges centerpiece and first-edition uncertainty.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if route planning, commercial self-resupply, long mountain blocks, and a six-day clock are the challenge you want. Wait for more editions if proven course continuity matters more than novelty.
final_verdict.alternatives: Choose the standard Utrecht Ultra for a 1,000 km and 100-hour version of the same format, or Race Around the Netherlands for a longer fixed-loop Dutch ultra.

eligibility.notes: New relevant race discovered during the Roadie Labs final source audit and added under the standing catalog rule. The inaugural competitive self-supported edition is currently running August 1-7, 2026 with a 1,600 km course, 14,000 m of climbing, mass start, solo and pairs categories, GPS tracking, and a 158-hour cutoff. The organizer has not published a 2027 date, registration cycle, checkpoints, parcours, or race manual, so the event is editorially eligible but source-blocked for a next-edition training fleet.

catalog_flags.status_note: This is a self-supported ultra-distance road race with mixed free routing and mandatory parcours, not a mass-participation gran fondo. The existing discipline enum is retained to avoid inventing schema; a future multi_stage or ultra_distance taxonomy should classify it explicitly.
